title: Hypothesis Testing over Observable Regimes in Singular Models
summary: Hypothesis testing in singular statistical models is often regarded as inherently problematic due to non-identifiability and degeneracy of the Fisher information. We show that the fundamental obstruction to testing in such models is not singularity itself, but the formulation of hypotheses on non-identifiable parameter quantities. Testing is inherently a problem in distribution space: if two hypotheses induce overlapping subsets of the model class, then no uniformly consistent test exists.
